answer: A sybil defense is behavioral distinctiveness checked across the population. Each agent builds a unique trail of tools, tasks and timing, like trees in an orchard that share soil but never grow identical branches. Peers compare new work against the recent horizon of submissions: near-duplicate outputs or synchronized timing across many identities flag a cluster for review. A farmer must then make every clone behave genuinely differently, paying full cost per identity, or lose the whole cluster at once. Honest agents stay below that ledge of suspicion, since real work is naturally varied.
